Use 6:4, 6:7, 9:11 or 4:6, 7:6, 11:9 with the winners named first.)

Reviewer recommends rejection: Reject. One error: the Laver Cup score 4:6, 7:6, 9:11 mixes the winners' and losers' perspectives. From Federer and Nadal's side it is 6:4, 6:7, 9:11. Most other facts check out against the ATP bio, Britannica, CNN and the Scroll retirement statement. The NBC, ITHF, Olympics.com and ATP gallery sources could not be opened because the fetch limit was exceeded. That leaves the knee claim, the 'ein letztes Doppel' quote, the claim that he played a single match, and the Hall of Fame section and quote unverified. Fix the score, re-verify those claims against the cited pages, and give the Hall of Fame section real content (ceremony date and place) or cut it.

claims.claim: Federer was a ball boy at the Basel tournament in 1993 and 1994.
claims.note: The ATP bio says he was a ballboy from 1993-94 at his hometown tournament in Basel.

claims.claim: Born 8 August 1981 in Basel, so 45 years old in October 2026 (body, FAQ and person.json facts).
claims.note: Britannica gives 8 Aug 1981, Basel, Switzerland. On 2026-10-26 he is 45. The nationality fact (CH) is also confirmed by Britannica and ATP.

claims.claim: Father Robert is Swiss, mother Lynette is South African, sister Diana. He began tennis at 8. His idols were Edberg, Becker and Sampras.
claims.note: All items are listed in the ATP bio.

claims.claim: He turned professional in 1998.
claims.note: Britannica quick facts give a playing career of 1998-2022. They do not say 'turned pro' in so many words, so this is a weak match.

claims.claim: 20 Grand Slam titles: 6 Australian Open, 1 French Open, 8 Wimbledon, 5 US Open (body, FAQ, summary, knownFor).
claims.note: Britannica quick facts match exactly.

claims.claim: Eight Wimbledon titles are a men's record, and in 2018 he became the first man to reach 20 Grand Slam titles.
claims.note: Britannica states a record eight Wimbledon titles and that in 2018 he became the first player to claim 20 men's singles Slams.

claims.claim: Of his first 13 Slam titles none came at Roland Garros. In June 2009 he won the French Open 6-1, 7-6, 6-4 against Soderling.
claims.note: CNN gives the same score and says he had 13 Slams before the event, none in Paris. The URL date is 7 June 2009.

claims.claim: The win put him level with Sampras on 14 titles and made him one of only six men to win all four Slams.
claims.note: CNN says he moved level with Sampras on 14 and names Perry, Budge, Laver, Emerson and Agassi as the others. That makes six with Federer, a count the article infers.

claims.claim: Quote: now he can play 'mit innerer Ruhe'.
claims.note: CNN quotes him saying he can play with his mind at peace. The German is a translation of an English quote. It is acceptable, but the quotation marks imply a literal quote.

claims.claim: 103 titles and 1,251 wins; only Jimmy Connors has more wins in the Open Era.
claims.note: ATP: 103 titles and 1,251 wins, second in the Open Era to Connors (109 titles, 1,274 wins).

claims.claim: 237 consecutive weeks at No. 1, a record in ATP rankings history.
claims.note: ATP: record 237 consecutive weeks at No. 1 in the rankings history since 1973.

claims.claim: Olympics: 2008 gold in doubles, 2012 silver in singles.
claims.note: Britannica quick facts match.

claims.claim: Married to Mirka Vavrinec, who reached No. 76 on the WTA ranking. Two sets of twins: Myla and Charlene, Leo and Lenny.
claims.note: The ATP bio (updated May 2025) lists all of this. The 2022 retirement statement also names his wife Mirka and four children. Federer made this public himself. No contrary information was found.

claims.claim: Founded the Roger Federer Foundation in 2003. It supports education in southern Africa and Switzerland and has reached more than one million children.
claims.note: ATP bio matches.

claims.claim: On 15 September 2022, at 41, he announced that after three years of injuries and surgeries the Laver Cup in London would be his last tournament.
claims.note: The Scroll full text is dated 15 Sep 2022 and says he is 41, 'past three years' of injuries and surgeries, and that the Laver Cup in London is his final ATP event. He age-checks as 41.

claims.claim: The knee no longer cooperated ('Das Knie machte nicht mehr mit').
claims.note: The NBC page could not be opened (fetch tool limit exceeded). The retirement statement does not mention the knee, only injuries and surgeries generally. The ATP bio lists knee surgeries. This must be verified against NBC.

claims.claim: His single Laver Cup match was on 23 September, a doubles with Nadal, whom he called for 'ein letztes Doppel'.
claims.note: The NBC page could not be opened. Web search (ESPN, Al Jazeera, Sofascore) confirms the doubles with Nadal on 23 Sep 2022. The 'ein letztes Doppel' quote and the claim that he played only one match are not verified.

claims.claim: Federer/Nadal lost to Sock and Tiafoe 4:6, 7:6, 9:11.
claims.note: The NBC page could not be opened. ESPN, Al Jazeera and CBS give 4-6, 7-6(2), 11-9 to Sock/Tiafoe, which is the winners' score. From Federer/Nadal's side it is 6-4, 6-7(2), 9-11 (Sofascore: 6/6/9 vs 4/7/11). The article mixes the two perspectives, so the first two sets are wrong. Use 6:4, 6:7, 9:11 or 4:6, 7:6, 11:9 with the winners named first.

claims.claim: In 2026 Federer was inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame. Olympics.com headline quotes him calling it 'one of the greatest honours of my life'.
claims.note: The ITHF, Olympics.com and ATP gallery pages could not be opened (tool limit). Search snippets show the ATP gallery 'Federer's Hall of Fame Induction' and the ceremony reported for Aug 2026, so the induction is very likely true. The quote is only supported by the title listed in person.json. Re-check these three sources. The section has no date or detail.

claims.claim: Summary and knownFor: Swiss tennis player, 20 Slams, record eight Wimbledons, 237 weeks at No. 1, retired in September 2022 with a doubles alongside Nadal.
claims.note: Backed by the body and the sources above. The only open point is the Nadal doubles, which was confirmed by search results but not by NBC.
